title: NADH-linked microtiter plate-based assay for measuring Rubisco activity
author: Cristina Rodrigues Gabriel Sales
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgasjsee
materials: REAGENTS & SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE BEFOREHAND Powder chemical stocks stored at -20°C: let warm up to room temperature on desiccant before opening container. Expensive chemicals purchased in very small amounts (mg), for which concentration in assay is not critical (e.g. in excess): trust quantity stated by the supplier and add ultrapure H 2 O / solvent to container for final concentration (e.g. PCK). Protein and substrate solutions should typically be stored at -80°C. Freeze proteins in LN 2 before storing at -80°C. Store in small aliquots to prevent multiple freeze-thaw cycles. If using in consecutive days, protein solutions can be kept at 4°C. Buffers and solutions will last longer if filtered through 0.22 µm membrane.

Please, check notes in section 2.1 to a more efficient way of aliquoting NADH. 1.8 KU/ml PCK Dissolve all solid by adding 100 Molarity (M) Bicine-NaOH pH 8 to the container; aliquot. -80 °C, (storage) 5 KU/ml GAPDH Dissolve all solid by adding 100 Molarity (M) Bicine-NaOH pH 8 to the container; aliquot. -80 °C, (storage) 17.9 KU/ml PGK Store at 4 °C when in ammonium sulfate suspension. SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE JUST BEFORE USE Prepared with reagents/solutions described in step 1.

START Thaw the frozen solutions that will be used in the day. Prepare CO 2 -free ultrapure H 2 O by bubbling with nitrogen (5 min/100 mL). Turn on the microplate reader and set up for the temperature that Rubisco activity will be performed, select kinetic protocol at 340 nm. The temperature to be used for the Rubisco activity measurement depends on the experiment goals. Typical measurement temperatures are 25 °C (standard) and 30 °C , depending on the species. Assays can be performed at a range of temperatures, however high temperatures might lead to evaporation of the assay mix and, since rates will be faster, the assay might become less sensitive. Turn on the centrifuge and set to 4 °C . Collect samples from -80 °C into liquid nitrogen container. Prepare the complete extraction buffer (from step 3.1) and the complete assay buffer (from step 3.2) and keep it On ice .

REAGENTS & SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE BEFOREHAND Powder chemical stocks stored at -20°C: let warm up to room temperature on desiccant before opening container. Expensive chemicals purchased in very small amounts (mg), for which concentration in assay is not critical (e.g. in excess): trust quantity stated by the supplier and add ultrapure H 2 O / solvent to container for final concentration (e.g. PCK). Protein and substrate solutions should typically be stored at -80°C. Freeze proteins in LN 2 before storing at -80°C. Store in small aliquots to prevent multiple freeze-thaw cycles. If using in consecutive days, protein solutions can be kept at 4°C. Buffers and solutions will last longer if filtered through 0.22 µm membrane.

steps.title: Prepare Stock Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following stock solutions and store as indicated:

substeps.instruction: Basic extraction buffer (1x): 50 mM Bicine-NaOH pH 8.2, 20 mM MgCl2.6H2O, 1 mM EDTA, 2 mM Benzamidine, 5 mM ε-Aminocaproic acid. Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, adjust pH to 8.2 with NaOH, degas by bubbling with nitrogen (5 min/10 mL), then add 50 mM 2-Mercaptoethanol. Store at -20 °C.
1 M DTT: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O. Store at 4 °C.
100 mM PMSF: Dissolve in ethanol 99%. Store at 4 °C.
20 mM RuBP (≥99% purity): Store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Complete Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix the following components on ice to create the complete extraction buffer:

substeps.instruction: Combine Basic extraction buffer (1x), 10 mM DTT, 1 mM PMSF, and 1% (v/v) Plant protease inhibitor cocktail.
Prepare a volume based on the number of extractions needed for the day plus two extra aliquots.

steps.title: Prepare Complete Assay Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the NADH-containing assay buffer on ice:

substeps.instruction: Thaw the basic assay buffer and NADH aliquots on ice.
Mix the required volumes of assay buffer and NADH together.
Keep the mixture on ice and wrapped in aluminium foil to protect the light-sensitive NADH.

steps.title: Set Up Microtiter Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare the 96-well plate before starting the extraction process:

substeps.instruction: Pipette 150.5 µL CO2-free ultrapure H2O into the blank well (singlet).
Pipette 144.5 µL CO2-free ultrapure H2O into each sample well (6 wells: triplicates for initial and triplicates for total activity).
Add 44.5 µL of complete assay buffer to each sample well.
Gently mix by pipetting up and down 5 times while stirring.
Add 6 µL of 20 mM RuBP to the wells designated for initial Rubisco activity.
Cover the plate to protect from light.

steps.title: Extract Rubisco Enzyme
steps.instruction: Perform rapid extraction of the enzyme to prevent deactivation:

substeps.instruction: Add complete extraction buffer to an ice-cold mortar.
Add a sample from liquid nitrogen and grind thoroughly for 30 to 60 seconds.
Collect the homogenate into an ice-cold 1.5 mL microtube.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 1 minute at 4 °C.
Immediately transfer the supernatant into another ice-cold 1.5 mL microtube.

steps.title: Perform Rubisco Activity Assay
steps.instruction: Measure the NADH-linked activity using a microplate reader at 340 nm and 30 °C:

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL of sample supernatant to the 'total activity' wells first, then to the 'initial activity' wells, mixing by pipetting up and down 10 times while stirring.
Immediately place the plate in the reader and monitor absorbance at 340 nm.
For total activity wells, incubate for 3 minutes at 30 °C to allow carbamylation.
After 3 minutes, pause the reading and add 6 µL of 20 mM RuBP to the total activity wells.
Resume monitoring absorbance until the reaction reaches a plateau.
